defects.description: The role-27 'silence = veto' check never fires for a model that follows the prompt. PROMPT_27 tells the model 'Never leave a field empty: write "not stated in rules" where it is silent', but parse_27 vetoes only empty strings. An answer with resolution_source='not stated in rules' and cutoff_time='not stated in rules' plus verdict 'clear' parses as ('clear', []) (probe P1). In practice, silence on a material point is vetoed only through the LLM's own verdict, while the roles doc says 'silence on any material point counts as a veto'. The test fixture CLEAR27 itself clears with cancellation_rule='not stated in rules'. This is still within the dispatch wording ('missing or empty'), and two qualified vendors plus role 28 must all clear. It is also not wired yet, which is why it is rated minor.
defects.fix_hint: In parse_27, treat a point whose answer is 'not stated in rules' (case-insensitive) as silent -> veto. Have the prompt use 'not applicable' for points that don't apply to the market type. Change CLEAR27.cancellation_rule to 'not applicable' and add one test for the sentinel.

defects.description: LLMGateway.complete() can raise despite 'it never raises'. n = max(0, int(vendors)) runs outside the try, so vendors=None gives a TypeError (probe P2). This only affects a caller passing the wrong type, since the Protocol types vendors as int.
defects.fix_hint: Move the int() conversion inside the try, or fall back to n=1 on a bad value.

defects.description: The signer can list three vendor/model pairs. When roles 27 and 28 are answered by different vendor pairs (for example after cache hits), the signer becomes 'llm-board:gemini/...+groq/...+openrouter/...' (probe P4e) instead of the dispatch's 'llm-board:<v1>/<m1>+<v2>/<m2>'. The record still loads and verifies, and the kernel does not parse signer.
defects.fix_hint: Accept and document the n-pair signer, or record the per-role pairs, e.g. 'llm-board:27=v1/m1+v2/m2;28=...'.

No real orders: board.py and gateway.py have no order, router, cancel, redeem or venue code. The only signature is an HMAC clearance record via trader.kernel.sign under env ROSTER_ADVISOR_KEY. It is refused when that key is missing, when it equals ROSTER_HUMAN_KEY, or when the db resolves to data/trader/advice.db. No authenticated venue endpoint is touched.

No real LLM or paid calls: all vendor HTTP goes through an injected transport. The tests use only a fake Transport or FakeGateway behind an autouse socket guard. The builder's real run had no keys, so it sent 0 requests: the gateway.db quota table is empty and the cache has 0 rows. Vendor keys are read from env at call time and sent in headers (Gemini uses x-goog-api-key, not the URL query). Transport errors log only the exception type.

No network in tests; no look-ahead applies. AI output cannot raise edge or size: the board only withholds or produces a clearance, and kernel acceptance is a later human-token Phase 1 change.
